label: end of input in long sequences (delimiter of L>=8), stronger when the sequence starts with w/k/q/2/a/g/l/n
explanation: Fires only at late steps of the original/delimiter phase and never during the copy phase. 70% of the activation mass is on the <DEL> step and the rest is on the last 1-3 original tokens (orig_idx 5-8, mostly first occurrences of a token); nothing fires at t<5. The rate rises steeply with absolute step and with L: 0 for L<=5, 0.4% of steps for L=7, 2.5% for L=9, and 14% of the steps with to_go=8 (the L=9 delimiter). Within those positions, whether it fires depends on sequence content, mainly the first original token (w, k, q, 2, a, g, l, n give 2-4x lift) and to a lesser degree orig(1). (t>=7)&(phase<=1) covers 97% of the mass but has only 12% precision. Adding the first-token condition brings dev precision to 0.59 but recall falls to 0.42 (F1 0.49), so the content dependence is only roughly captured.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: w, q, k, a, 2, g; least: m, z, h, f) and the next token to output (most: k, g, w, 2, q, p; least: h, 0, 1, m); timing cues that raise it most: t=7, L=9 & t=9, t=8.
